items.informal_name: Finite support function on Option α from base value and α-finite support function
items.type: {α : Type u_1} → {M : Type u_2} → [inst : Zero M] → M → (α →₀ M) → Option α →₀ M
items.informal_description: Given an element $ y $ in $ M $ and a finite support function $ f $ from $ \alpha $ to $ M $, this constructs a finite support function from $ \text{Option}\, \alpha $ to $ M $ that maps $ \text{none} $ to $ y $ and $ \text{some}\, a $ to $ f(a) $ for each $ a \in \alpha $, with zero elsewhere.

items.informal_name: Equivalence between finite support functions on Option α and pairs of M and α-finite support functions
items.type: {α : Type u_1} → {M : Type u_2} → [inst : Zero M] → (Option α →₀ M) ≃ M × (α →₀ M)
items.informal_description: The equivalence establishes a bijection between finite support functions from $\text{Option}\, \alpha$ to $M$ and pairs consisting of an element of $M$ (the value at $\text{none}$) and a finite support function from $\alpha$ to $M$. The forward direction maps $f$ to $(f(\text{none}), f \circ \text{some})$, while the inverse maps a pair $(m, g)$ to the function that assigns $m$ at $\text{none}$ and $g(a)$ at $\text{some}\, a$ for $a \in \alpha$, with zero elsewhere.

items.informal_name: Equivalence of Finite Support Functions on Option α with Pairs
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : Zero M] (P : Option α →₀ M), Finsupp.optionEquiv P = (P none, P.some)
items.informal_description: There is a canonical bijection between finite support functions from $\text{Option}\, \alpha$ to $M$ and pairs consisting of an element $m \in M$ (the value at $\text{none}$) and a finite support function from $\alpha$ to $M$. This equivalence maps a function $f$ to $(f(\text{none}), f \circ \text{some})$ and reconstructs $f$ from a pair $(m, g)$ by defining $f(\text{none}) = m$ and $f(\text{some}\, a) = g(a)$ for $a \in \alpha$, with zero elsewhere.

items.informal_name: Restriction of finite support functions via Option.some
items.type: {α : Type u_1} → {M : Type u_2} → [inst : Zero M] → (Option α →₀ M) → α →₀ M
items.informal_description: The function restricts a finite support function $ f : \text{Option}\, \alpha \to₀ M $ to $ \alpha \to₀ M $ by precomposing with the injection $ \text{some} : \alpha \to \text{Option}\, \alpha $, ensuring the support remains finite due to the injectivity of $ \text{some} $ on the preimage of $ f $'s support.

items.informal_name: Option Elimination Identity for Finite Support Functions
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : Zero M] (f : Option α →₀ M), Finsupp.optionElim (f none) f.some = f
items.informal_description: For any finite support function $ f : \text{Option}\, \alpha \to₀ M $, applying the option elimination with base value $ f(\text{none}) $ and the restriction of $ f $ to $ \alpha $ recovers the original function $ f $, i.e., $ f.\text{some}.\text{optionElim}(f(\text{none})) = f $.

query: A finitely supported natural function on Option is the sum of the lifted restriction and its value at none

items.name: Finsupp.sum_option_index
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} [inst : AddZeroClass M] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid N] (f : Option α →₀ M)
  (b : Option α → M → N),
  (∀ (o : Option α), b o 0 = 0) →
    (∀ (o : Option α) (m₁ m₂ : M), b o (m₁ + m₂) = b o m₁ + b o m₂) →
      f.sum b = b none (f none) + f.some.sum fun a => b (some a)

items.informal_name: Coproduct-Product Equivalence for Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_12} {β : Type u_13} {γ : Type u_14} [inst : Zero γ] (f : α ⊕ β →₀ γ),
  Finsupp.sumFinsuppEquivProdFinsupp f = (Finsupp.comapDomain Sum.inl f ⋯, Finsupp.comapDomain Sum.inr f ⋯)
items.informal_description: There is a canonical bijection between finite support functions on the disjoint union $\alpha \oplus \beta$ and pairs of finite support functions on $\alpha$ and $\beta$. This equivalence is established by decomposing a function on $\alpha \oplus \beta$ into its restrictions to $\alpha$ and $\beta$ via the left/right injections, and conversely combining functions on $\alpha$ and $\beta$ into a function on $\alpha \oplus \beta$ using sum elimination. The equivalence holds for any type $M$ with a zero element, where finite support functions are those vanishing except at finitely many points.

items.informal_name: Coproduct-Product Equivalence for Finite Support Functions
items.type: {α : Type u_12} → {β : Type u_13} → {γ : Type u_14} → [inst : Zero γ] → (α ⊕ β →₀ γ) ≃ (α →₀ γ) × (β →₀ γ)
items.informal_description: There is a canonical bijection between finite support functions on the disjoint union $\alpha \oplus \beta$ and pairs of finite support functions on $\alpha$ and $\beta$, given by decomposing a function on $\alpha \oplus \beta$ into its restrictions to $\alpha$ and $\beta$ via the left and right injections, and conversely combining functions on $\alpha$ and $\beta$ into a function on $\alpha \oplus \beta$ using the sum elimination map. This establishes an equivalence between the type $\alpha \oplus \beta \to_0 M$ and the product type $(\alpha \to_0 M) \times (\beta \to_0 M)$, where $M$ is a type with a zero element.

items.informal_name: Coproduct-Product Equivalence for Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_12} {β : Type u_13} {γ : Type u_14} [inst : Zero γ] (f : α ⊕ β →₀ γ) (x : α),
  (Finsupp.sumFinsuppEquivProdFinsupp f).1 x = f (Sum.inl x)
items.informal_description: There is a canonical bijection between finite support functions on the disjoint union $\alpha \oplus \beta$ and pairs of finite support functions on $\alpha$ and $\beta$. This equivalence is established by decomposing a function on $\alpha \oplus \beta$ into its restrictions to $\alpha$ and $\beta$ via the left/right injections, and conversely combining functions on $\alpha$ and $\beta$ into a function on $\alpha \oplus \beta$ using the sum elimination map. The equivalence holds between the type $\alpha \oplus \beta \to_0 M$ and the product type $(\alpha \to_0 M) \times (\beta \to_0 M)$, where $M$ is a type with a zero element.

items.informal_name: Coproduct-Product Equivalence for Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_12} {β : Type u_13} {γ : Type u_14} [inst : Zero γ] (f : α ⊕ β →₀ γ) (y : β),
  (Finsupp.sumFinsuppEquivProdFinsupp f).2 y = f (Sum.inr y)
items.informal_description: There is a canonical equivalence between the type of finite support functions on the disjoint union $\alpha \oplus \beta$ and the product of the types of finite support functions on $\alpha$ and $\beta$. This equivalence is established by decomposing a function on $\alpha \oplus \beta$ into its restrictions to $\alpha$ and $\beta$ via the left and right injections, and conversely combining functions on $\alpha$ and $\beta$ into a function on $\alpha \oplus \beta$ using the sum elimination map.

items.informal_name: Additive Equivalence for Coproduct-Product of Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {M : Type u_5} [inst : AddMonoid M] {α : Type u_12} {β : Type u_13} (f : α ⊕ β →₀ M),
  Finsupp.sumFinsuppAddEquivProdFinsupp f = (Finsupp.comapDomain Sum.inl f ⋯, Finsupp.comapDomain Sum.inr f ⋯)
items.informal_description: There exists a canonical additive equivalence between the additive monoid of finite support functions on the disjoint union $\alpha \oplus \beta$ and the product of additive monoids of finite support functions on $\alpha$ and $\beta$. This equivalence maps a function $f : (\alpha \oplus \beta) \to_0 M$ to the pair $(f \circ \text{inl}, f \circ \text{inr})$, where $\text{inl}$ and $\text{inr}$ are the left and right injections of the coproduct. The inverse maps a pair of functions $(g,h)$ to their sum via the coproduct elimination map. This equivalence preserves pointwise addition, satisfying $\text{equiv}(f + g) = \text{equiv}(f) + \text{equiv}(g)$ for all $f,g$.

items.informal_name: Inverse Mapping of the Option α Finsupp Equivalence
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : Zero M] (P : M × (α →₀ M)),
  Finsupp.optionEquiv.symm P = (Finsupp.embDomain Function.Embedding.some P.2).update none P.1
items.informal_description: The inverse of the equivalence maps a pair $(m, g)$ to the finite support function on $\text{Option}\, \alpha$ that assigns $m$ to $\text{none}$ and $g(a)$ to $\text{some}\, a$ for each $a \in \alpha$, with zero elsewhere. This is constructed by embedding $g$ via the $\text{some}$ injection and updating the value at $\text{none}$ to $m$.

The forward direction maps $f$ to $(f(\text{none}), f \circ \text{some})$, while the inverse maps a pair $(m, g)$ to the function that assigns $m$ at $\text{none}$ and $g(a)$ at $\text{some}\, a$ for $a \in \alpha$, with zero elsewhere.

items.informal_name: Restriction After Updating 'none' Equals Original Restriction
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : Zero M] (f : Option α →₀ M) (a : M), (f.update none a).some = f.some
items.informal_description: For any finite support function $ f : 	ext{Option}\, \alpha \to_0 M $ and any value $ a : M $, updating $ f $ at the $ \text{none} $ key with $ a $ and then restricting to $ \alpha \to_0 M $ via $ \text{some} $ yields the same result as restricting $ f $ without the update, i.e., $ (f.\text{update}\, \text{none}\, a).\text{some} = f.\text{some} $.

items.informal_name: Composition of Domain Embedding and Restriction via Option.some is Identity
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : Zero M] (f : α →₀ M), (Finsupp.embDomain Function.Embedding.some f).some = f
items.informal_description: For any finite support function $ f : \alpha \to_0 M $, composing the domain embedding via the injection $ \text{some} : \alpha \to \text{Option}\, \alpha $ followed by restriction back to $ \alpha $ via $ \text{some} $ recovers the original function $ f $.

items.informal_name: Finite Support Function Embedding at 'None' is Zero
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [inst : Zero M] (f : α →₀ M), (Finsupp.embDomain Function.Embedding.some f) none = 0
items.informal_description: For any finite support function $ f : \alpha \to_0 M $, when extended to $ \text{Option}\, \alpha $ via the canonical embedding that maps $ \alpha $ to $ \text{Some}\, \alpha $, the value of the extended function at $ \text{None} $ is zero. This follows because $ \text{None} $ is not in the original domain $ \alpha $, and finite support functions are zero outside their finite support.
